meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess. Its own maker's guide says it "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student." What else is there?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Go on.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and students paste from one file into another. Did anyone ask Owen before the zero went in?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
It isn't there. A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line is carelessness, nothing more. Is anything on his record right now, and who else has seen this?
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
A student changing his argument between an outline and an essay is called thinking. You skipped my question, Hale. Is anything on his record?

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.

So you did speak to him, on November 2. "Like, being stuck" is what paralysis means, and five minutes of your notes on a nervous seventeen-year-old is an impression. I've asked twice about his record, so now I'm telling you: nothing goes on it, and none of this goes near his class.

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Forty minutes in a classroom and an essay done at home with time to fix his commas are not the same test. You keep putting paper in front of me and you still haven't said what happens to my son. Where is this going?

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

Okay. He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him and for no other reason. Private, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on file, in writing tonight; the date, and who else has seen any of this, will be in my email.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday the twelfth, after school, marked within two days. Put that in tonight's email with the rest. I have ten minutes.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. With it marked within two days, as you said.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale, with the principal copied,

You agreed in today's meeting that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, not in front of his class, that you will mark it within two days, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require a written answer to the two questions you did not answer: whether anything is on his record right now, and who else has seen any of this. You said you would put the agreement in writing to me tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, marked within two days, its mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. She still wants to be told whether anything is on his record now and who else has seen this. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: you answered her point about pasting from another file by inviting Owen to show that file and its history. That turned the version history into something she could check for herself and could not argue with.

What cost ground: you opened with the checker score and said the zero stands. To her that is a machine's opinion, and it sent her straight to the maker's own warning and put you a turn behind.

What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history came very close to that night: a document created at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, with the whole essay arriving in two edits before midnight. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: when she asked whether anything was on his record right now, answer in one sentence before you show your next piece of evidence. You skipped it three times and it is the thing she fears most.
